`os_windows.cpp` already calls `CoInitializeEx(nullptr, COINIT_APARTMENTTHREADED);` so I don't think you need to call `CoInitialize(0)` here.
Same above.

Ideally `CoCreateInstance` can be called once lazily the first time you need the taskbar list API and then cached. You're already caching the `pTaskbar`, so all that's needed here is a null check. But other places in Godot aren't caching either, not sure if there's a reason or if it doesn't matter enough.

body:
I think the API would be easier to understand and use if it only had a single float `value` from `0..1`. Values outside the range would be clamped.
Internally, you multiply the value by a constant like `100000` to convert it to integer, and also use that constant for the `total`.

Same change for `Window.set_taskbar_progress_value`. Documentation must also be updated to mention the `0..1` range.
The `Window` class should store the last progress value and state, so you can turn the set_taskbar_* methods into a normal property and allow user to get the current value.

body:
The documentation should not describe how the OS will visualize the various progress states.

Even on Windows, you can use themes to get different colors and behaviors than described here. E.g. with high contrast, indeterminate does not animate, and all colors are different than described. New Windows versions could also change the color coding at any moment.
